scoring_justification: DFT adsorption energies are the final computed output; recompute from raw artifacts is impossible in the verifier sandbox, so we compare the agent's reported values to the paper's gold with a tolerance of ±0.3 eV and verify four structural ordering trends.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper-reported Li adsorption energies for the six molecular models
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Extracted from the paper text (Figure 5 and main text): bowl C30H10 inner −2.51 eV, flat C30H14 −1.88 eV, C60 inner −2.41 eV, C60 outer −2.31 eV, C54N4 all‑N5 −5.56 eV, C54N4 two N5+two N6 −6.03 eV.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Manual extraction from the published paper
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values are directly from the paper's reported DFT‑D2 results and match the reference solve.sh exactly; they are not invented.

outputs.description: Lithium adsorption energies computed with DFT-D2 for the five molecular models. The values are compared to the paper-reported values and checked for structural trends (curved > flat, N-doped > undoped, mixed doping > all-N5) using hidden tolerances.

output_contract.notes: The hidden checker reads the agent's reported energies and compares each value to the paper's reference within ±0.3 eV, then verifies the following structural relationships: (1) bowl_C30H10_inner < flat_C30H14 (curved binds stronger), (2) both C54N4 entries < C60_inner, (3) C54N4_two_N5_two_N6 < C54N4_all_N5.

steps.description: Validate Li adsorption energies against paper reference and structural trends

trends.description: all-N5 doping enhances binding relative to undoped C60
two N5+two N6 doping enhances binding relative to undoped C60
mixed N5+N6 doping stronger than all-N5
